## Natural history notes

A slender medium-sized shorebird characterized by long bright yellow legs, gray-brown upperparts, white underparts, a thin straight dark bill, and a nervous, active feeding style. In Florida, the Lesser Yellowlegs is found mainly as a migrant and winter visitor in shallow wetlands, mudflats, marshes, flooded fields, lake edges, impoundments, mangrove edges, and coastal lagoons. It feeds by walking through shallow water and picking or sweeping for small insects, crustaceans, worms, snails, and other aquatic invertebrates.
